cover.title: When clouds close in, the lakes stay in view.
cover.lede: Pakistan's glacial lakes fill and burst in summer, when cloud hides them from optical satellites. SARtale reads NASA–ISRO NISAR radar, which sees through cloud, and gives each lake one plain status.

risk.label: 01 · THE RISK
risk.title: One lake, one bridge, one morning
risk.body: On 7 May 2022 the ice-dammed lake below Shisper glacier burst. Its flood ran 6.4 km down the Hassanabad gorge and destroyed the Karakoram Highway bridge, Hunza's link to the rest of the country.
risk.source: Sources: Radio Pakistan, 7 May 2022. The 6.4 km is the straight line from the register point to OpenStreetMap way 651792498.

gap.quote: Persistent cloud cover after 16 June 2026 has limited the availability of cloud-free satellite imagery, making it difficult to accurately assess lake area changes during the last three to four days.

shadow.title: Mountains cast shadows too
shadow.lede: Glacial lakes sit in deep, steep valleys. Shadow can hide a lake from both kinds of satellite, and a dark shadow can be mistaken for water.

cards.label: OPTICAL SATELLITES
cards.text: The sun's shadow falls across slopes and valley floors. A shaded lake can be missed, and a shaded slope can look like water.

cards.label: RADAR
cards.text: Radar looks sideways. Slopes facing away from the satellite fall in radar shadow, and steep slopes facing it fold over (layover). Both can hide a shoreline.

cards.label: WHAT SARTALE DOES
cards.text: NISAR passes over each lake from two directions. A pixel dark from only one side is shadow, not water, and is left out. If less than {minObservable} of a lake's zone can be seen, it reads Not observable instead of a guess.

measure.title: Dark radar pixels become a water area
measure.imageAlt: {attabadName} in NISAR radar on {attabadDate}, with the water SARtale reads shown in blue

measure.caption: {attabadDate}, track {attabadTrack}. Blue: water read from radar, inside the lake outline (OpenStreetMap).
steps: Calm water reflects radar away, so it is dark in both HH and HV.
Mountain shadow is dark from one viewing direction only, so it is removed.
What is left is counted inside the lake's zone and compared with its own earlier passes.

add.label: 06 · ADD A LAKE
add.title: Know a lake we are not watching?
add.body: Give it a name, its coordinates and where they come from. SARtale searches NASA's catalogue for NISAR passes over it, reads a 6 km window from each, and gives it a status once it has {minLooks} looks on one track.
steps: Requested: the request opens as a GitHub issue.
Searched: NISAR passes over the point are counted.
Watched: once the team accepts it, a status appears after {minLooks} looks on one track.
